newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN health agency rejects Taiwan bid as observer.
newsitem.headline: UN health agency rejects Taiwan bid as observer.

text.p: The head of the World Health Organisation (WHO) has rejected Taiwan's request for observer status as no such category exists at the U.N. health agency, a WHO spokesman said on Thursday.

Chief spokesman Richard LeClair told Reuters Hiroshi Nakajima, WHO's Japanese director-general, also decided against using his discretion to invite Taiwan to attend the World Health Assembly next month as an observer.

This was because Taiwan lacked status under international law, its application was controversial and a United Nations General Assembly resolution of 1971 transferred China's U.N. seat from Taipei to Beijing, LeClair said.
But if one of WHO's 191 member states proposed inviting Taiwan to the annual forum, and the resolution were adopted, Nakajima would invite Taipei, he added.

In this case, Taiwan could follow in the steps of the African National Congress (ANC) and Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) and receive observer status to attend the annual talks, normally the following year.
The Geneva-based WHO holds its annual session from May 5-14.

Taiwan said on Wednesday it had applied to become an observer at WHO and urged Beijing not to block its bid to take part in what Foreign Minister John Chang called the least politically sensitive U.N. body.

China, which has regarded Taiwan as a rebel-held province ineligible for international recognition since a civil war split them in 1949, has blocked Taipei's membership as a sovereign state in all international forums since taking the U.N. seat.
